documents.sanskrit: जीवात्मनः परमात्मा हि अंशभूतो हि जायते
documents.transliteration: Jivatmanah paramatma hi ansha-bhuto hi jayate
documents.text: The individual soul is an eternal portion of the Supreme Consciousness, taking birth according to the fruits of past karmas.

documents.sanskrit: सूर्यो ब्रह्मा रविस्तद्वत् चन्द्रमा मनसः प्रभुः
documents.transliteration: Suryo brahma ravistadvat chandrama manasah prabhuh
documents.text: Surya is the soul (Atman) and life-force of all beings; Chandra is the ruler of the mind (Manas) and emotional currents.
Mangala (Mars) governs courage, vitality, and physical vigor; Budha (Mercury) is the supreme giver of discrimination, intellect, and speech.
Guru (Jupiter) bestows higher spiritual wisdom, discernment, and ethical expansion; Shukra (Venus) bestows artistic refinement, affection, and aesthetic beauty.

Shani (Saturn) teaches endurance, humility, and karmic justice through delay and discipline; Rahu brings worldly illusions and unconventional breakthroughs; Ketu brings spiritual detachment and Moksha.
The First House (Tanu Bhava / Lagna) governs physical vitality, self-identity, constitution, and the life trajectory.
The Second House (Dhana Bhava) governs accumulated wealth, family lineage, truthfulness of speech, and right sustenance.
The Fourth House (Sukha Bhava) governs mother, inner peace of the heart, ancestral roots, shelter, and emotional security.
The Fifth House (Putra / Purva-Punya Bhava) governs creative intelligence, spiritual merit from past lives, mantric siddhi, and progeny.
The Ninth House (Dharma Bhava) is the supreme house of grace, governing righteous conduct, Guru, higher philosophy, pilgrimages, and fatherly blessings.
The Tenth House (Karma Bhava) governs worldly duty, righteous profession, leadership, public honour, and contribution to society.
The Twelfth House (Vyaya Bhava) governs spiritual liberation (Moksha), solitary contemplation, expenditure for sacred charity, and release from rebirth.

When Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, or Saturn occupy a Kendra in their own or exaltation sign, Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hamsa, Malavya, and Sasa Mahapurusha yogas are formed, bestowing nobility of character and enduring influence.
The planetary Dasha reflects the ripening of specific karmic seeds (Prarabdha). The Mahadasha lord sets the overarching life theme, while the Antardasha specifies the immediate arena of action.
Adverse planetary periods are balanced through Sattvic remedies: dedicated japa of planetary mantras, contemplation, charitable feeding (dana), pilgrimage, and disciplined non-harming (Ahimsa).
